Use the defining properties of `ComplexShape.EulerCharSigns` for the first conjunct: the sign character `χ : ι → ℤˣ` changes by negation across every relation `c.Rel i j`.

For the equivalence, view homology simply as a graded object. Then:

- The graded-object Euler-characteristic formula immediately gives the homology formula by applying it to \(X_i = H_i(C)\); their supports and Euler characteristics are definitionally the same.
- Conversely, realize any graded object \(X\) as a homological complex with objects \(X_i\) and all differentials zero. Its homology in degree \(i\) is canonically isomorphic to \(X_i\), so the assumed homology formula transfers to the desired graded-object formula.

The useful intermediate goals are that the zero-differential complex has homology of the required finite rank/support and that Euler characteristic and finrank are invariant under the resulting degreewise isomorphisms. The essential mechanism is thus the zero-differential realization of graded objects.
